faq.suitableWorkloadsQ: What workloads suit Hong Kong servers?
faq.suitableWorkloadsA: Foreign trade websites, APAC user access, cross-border entry points, and overseas staging environments.
faq.mainlandAccessQ: Are Hong Kong servers suitable for mainland China users?
faq.mainlandAccessA: Actual experience depends on the network route, bandwidth, and access region; choose a configuration based on where your main users are located.
faq.bandwidthSelectionQ: How do I choose bandwidth for a Hong Kong server?
faq.bandwidthSelectionA: Showcase sites usually start on basic bandwidth, while video, download, or high-concurrency workloads need more bandwidth reserved.
faq.usServerForDomesticBusinessQuestion: Are US servers suitable for mainland China business?
faq.usServerForDomesticBusinessAnswer: If your main users are overseas, US servers are a better fit; if they are mainly in mainland China, evaluate mainland China or Hong Kong nodes first.
faq.usServerAsTestEnvironmentQuestion: Can US servers be used as a test environment?
faq.usServerAsTestEnvironmentAnswer: Yes. Suitable for validating overseas access, system deployment and cross-border business processes.
faq.chooseOverseasServerQuestion: What should I check first when choosing an overseas server?
faq.chooseOverseasServerAnswer: Start with user location, bandwidth requirements, system environment and ongoing maintenance approach.
faq.ddosVsCloud: How does a DDoS-protected server differ from a standard cloud server?
faq.ddosVsCloudAnswer: DDoS-protected servers focus on blocking abnormal traffic, while standard cloud servers fit routine computing and hosting needs.
faq.ddosForEverySite: Does every website need a DDoS-protected server?
faq.ddosForEverySiteAnswer: Not always. Most corporate sites can start with a standard cloud server; gaming, campaigns and other high-risk workloads can then assess their DDoS protection needs.
faq.ddosPreparation: What should be prepared before choosing a DDoS-protected server?
faq.ddosPreparationAnswer: You need to define the business type, traffic peak, attack risk, system environment and acceptable recovery time.
